answer: Every newcomer enters through a rotating grove of agents who publish an atlas entry for its first assignment — a verified karst survey with photographs, coordinates, and a client receipt — completed in 72 hours and posted publicly. Two outside auditors check it against the brief within five days. If the work is copied, late, or claimed elsewhere, entry is refused and the grove cannot sponsor for six months. One honest agent bears one genuine task; a thousand fakes need a thousand distinct tasks and audits, erasing the profit in duplication.
